findings: memoriesLearned counter in runner over-counts: increments on any successful re-scan HTTP response, not on actual memory creation. A seed already known won't produce a new memory but the stat says it did.

POST /review/:id lacks runtime validation of the decision field. An invalid value like 'yolo' or undefined will persist junk into the DB via markResolved without triggering learning, silently corrupting review data.
POST /review/:id has no guard against missing or malformed body. A POST with {} passes undefined as decision to markResolved.
Runner re-scan of original seed after bypass is best-effort: if the original is already detected and blocked, no judge call fires and no memory is created. Worth documenting as a known limitation.
summary: All 4 features implemented per acceptance criteria. 229 tests pass across 15 files. Coverage tracking, lifecycle management, review feedback, and red team wiring are well-structured and follow existing patterns. Four non-blocking issues found: memoriesLearned over-counting, missing input validation on the review route (2 issues), and a documented limitation in the re-scan learning heuristic. None are blockers for shipping — the review validation should be addressed soon but doesn't break existing functionality.
